title: Controlled source pack for Ontario Class 4 Water Distribution remediation

sources.title: Safe Drinking Water Act, 2002, S.O. 2002, c. 32
sources.scope: Binding statute. Use for owner, operating authority, operator, licensing, operational plan, enforcement, and general legal framework questions only when a specific section is supplied. Do not assign an owner duty to every individual operator without the cited provision.

sources.title: O. Reg. 170/03: Drinking Water Systems
sources.scope: Binding regulation. Use for named system categories, sampling, operational checks, residual monitoring, adverse-result notification and corrective action only with the applicable schedule or section and stated system scope. Licence, permit, order, or approval conditions can be more stringent.

sources.title: O. Reg. 169/03: Ontario Drinking Water Quality Standards
sources.scope: Binding regulation. Use for a named Ontario drinking-water quality standard only with its correct schedule, unit, analyte, and statistical basis. Do not call nonbinding aesthetic objectives a requirement under this regulation.

sources.title: O. Reg. 128/04: Certification of Drinking Water System Operators and Water Quality Analysts
sources.scope: Binding regulation. Use for operator or water quality analyst certification. Class 4 certification demonstrates qualifications; it does not by itself allocate owner or overall management duties.

sources.title: Procedure for Disinfection of Drinking Water in Ontario
sources.scope: Official ministry technical procedure. Use for primary disinfection, CT, T10, residual location, and post-repair disinfection concepts. Do not invent detailed AWWA dose, contact-time, sampling, or acceptance values. Residual maintenance is not a CT question.

sources.title: Design Guidelines for Drinking-Water Systems: Instrumentation, Control and Distribution Systems
sources.scope: Official ministry design guidance. Use for hydraulics, water age, pressure zones, transients, looped systems, flushing provisions, and design analysis. Label guidance as guidance, not as a universal legal duty.

sources.title: O. Reg. 632/05: Confined Spaces
sources.scope: Binding Ontario occupational-health-and-safety regulation. Use only after the stem establishes a confined-space scenario. Test assessment, plan, isolation, entry authorization, atmospheric testing, monitoring, rescue, and training without presenting a single detector reading as proof of safe entry.

sources.title: Ontario's Drinking Water Quality Management Standard Pocket Guide
sources.scope: Official explanatory guide for quality-management, risk-assessment, emergency-preparedness, and internal-audit concepts. It is a summary, not a substitute for the governing law, regulation, Director's Direction, or site-specific instrument.

authoringControls: State Ontario and the system category whenever a legal duty, limit, frequency, or notification obligation is tested.
Distinguish a binding law or regulation from ministry guidance, a site-specific approval, or ordinary good practice.
Do not write a universal reporting, flushing, residual, pressure, disinfection, or operator-responsibility claim unless the source scope and facts support it.
Do not use a Class 4 certificate as proof of an assigned management role or personal legal duty.
For a calculation, provide all inputs, formula, units, assumptions, and a concise reproducible solution. Replace incomplete legacy calculations with non-calculation operational items.
Use four distinct, plausible options. Do not use all-of-the-above or none-of-the-above.
